description: Apply a whole patch in the apply_patch (V4A) format: the exact '*** Begin Patch' … '*** End Patch' format you know, with '*** Add File: ', '*** Delete File: ', '*** Update File: ' (+ optional '*** Move to: ') hunks, '@@ ' context markers, and ' '/'+'/'-' change lines. All-or-nothing: every hunk is validated and computed before anything is written — a context mismatch fails the whole call with C210 and the guidance to re-read and regenerate; on success each file commits atomically and modified files return a bounded post-apply echo of the first changed region. Paths are relative to the primary allowed root or absolute inside any allowed root (coder::info lists them); for host paths outside the jail use shell::fs::*.

examples.patch:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/calc.py
@@ def add(a, b):
-    return a - b
+    return a + b
*** End Patch

patch.description: The full patch text in the apply_patch format: starts with `*** Begin Patch`, ends with `*** End Patch`, with one hunk per file (`*** Add File: `, `*** Delete File: `, or `*** Update File: ` with an optional `*** Move to: `). Paths are relative to the primary allowed root, or absolute inside any allowed root.

from_line.description: 1-based line number of the first echoed line, post-apply.

echo.description: Bounded post-apply snapshot of the first changed region (modified files only) — verify from this instead of re-reading the file.

new_line_count.description: Line count after applying (absent for deletions).

path.description: Canonical absolute path of the affected file (the destination for a moved file).

results.description: One entry per file hunk, in patch order. The whole patch applied — a failure anywhere returns an error with nothing written.
